question: Daksh travels 200 km at 50 km/hr, the next 252 km at 42 km/hr and the next 204 km at 51 km/hr. What is his average speed (in km/hr) for the whole journey? (Round off your answer to two decimal places)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance = 200 + 252 + 204 = 656 km

Total time = (200 ÷ 50) + (252 ÷ 42) + (204 ÷ 51) = 4 + 6 + 4 = 14 hours

Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time

Average speed = 656 ÷ 14 = 46.857... ≈ 46.86 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 46.86 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance d₁ = 200 km, Speed s₁ = 50 km/hr

Distance d₂ = 252 km, Speed s₂ = 42 km/hr

Distance d₃ = 204 km, Speed s₃ = 51 km/hr

**Formulas Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken for the first part (t₁) = 200 ÷ 50 = 4 hours

⇒ Time taken for the second part (t₂) = 252 ÷ 42 = 6 hours

⇒ Time taken for the third part (t₃) = 204 ÷ 51 = 4 hours

⇒ Total Time = 4 + 6 + 4 = 14 hours

⇒ Total Distance = 200 + 252 + 204 = 656 km

⇒ Average Speed = 656 ÷ 14

⇒ Average Speed = 46.857... km/hr

⇒ Average Speed ≈ 46.86 km/hr (rounded off to two decimal places)

**∴ The correct answer is 46.86 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Two Equal Distances

If a person covers a certain distance at a speed of **a** km/hr and an equal distance at a speed of **b** km/hr, the average speed for the whole journey is given by: **2ab ÷ (a + b)**.

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

If three equal distances are covered at speeds of **a**, **b**, and **c** respectively, the average speed is: **3abc ÷ (ab + bc + ca)**.

Relative Speed

When two bodies are moving in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (v₁ − v₂). When moving in opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds (v₁ + v₂).
